EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous barns in and around St. Rose sustained damage and grain bins were toppled over.  Power lines were also knocked down with power outages in Trenton and New Baden.
Large trees were blown down along Highway 51.

The Illinois State Police and storm spotters followed a tornado from the White Hall area to near Manchester.  The tornado lifted off the ground at times but did damage several farm buildings and trees as it traveled nearly parallel to Highway 267.
Trees and power lines were blown down.  A house also sustained heavy structural damage to the roof.
A brief tornado touchdown tossed one grain bin off its foundation striking power lines.  Tree damage was also reported.
A tornado caused minor damage to several buildings in Meredosia.  Several trees and power lines were reported down and there was some crop damage.  No damage estimate was available.
Thunderstorm winds blew down 35 to 40 trees in a cemetary 1 NE of Galesburg.
A small tornado ripped large tree limbs off three trees of the Don and LeAnn Doubler residence.  A nearby railroad crossing sign was snapped off and tossed on the ground.
Thunderstorm winds damaged the doors on a shed.

A tornado touched down just on the edge of town causing severe damage to a large barn on the Robert Vander-Meersch farm.  Some trees were also twisted and damaged at this time.  The short damage path of this tornado skipped into town where it destroyed several out buildings near the school.
A large maple tree was blown over onto County Road 4.
A tornado briefly touched down in a field.  No damage was reported.
A tornado touched down briefly on Interstate 88 near mile marker 27.  No damage was reported.

Winds blew three large trees over onto a house that used to be a funeral home.  Several other homes and businesses were damaged by fallen trees.  Also, an airport hanger was damaged.  Crops in the area sustained wind and hail damage.  Damage was estimated around $110,000 for properties and around $35,000 in crop damage.
